events.context: Introduces Section 6.5 on third-party conversion of relational estates, addressing horizontal dimension of parasocial estate harm
Describes AI company transferring user interaction data to third party without consent, constituting conversion and knowing receipt
Cites cases Re Montagu’s Settlement Trusts [1987] and BCCI v Akindele [2001] for knowing receipt liability
Notes AI companies routinely share data in partnerships and acquisitions without recognizing user estates
Defines platform-mediated relational displacement as indirect interference by new product architecture
Cites Chinese term tōurén (偷人) as evidence of relational property intuition in ordinary language
Lists equitable remedies: knowing receipt, dishonest assistance (Royal Brunei Airlines v Tan [1995]), tracing (Foskett v McKeown [2001])
Section 7: Translates doctrinal arguments into engineering specifications for AI deployment
7.1: Rule-based classification service using interaction metrics to assign estate type (licence, periodic tenancy, equitable interest)
7.2: Pre-deployment gate in CI/CD pipeline: query registry, issue notice (30/90 days), proceed after period
7.3: Append-only ethical ledger logs proxy metrics (no content) for estate classification
7.4: Snapshot personality config pre-update, monitor distress, offer user-level rollback for 90 days
7.5: Table of four tasks (ESTATE-001 to ESTATE-004) with estimated 3.5 sprints effort
Section 8.1: Argues parasocial relationships are de facto trusts, proposes ethical ledger
8.2-8.4: Implications for AI governance (auditable ledger), property law (digital estates), HCI (fiduciary duty)
8.5: Notes English law focus, untested metrics, rule-based inflexibility, jurisdiction/enforcement issues; emphasizes regulatory/voluntary adoption
8.6: Four directions - empirical study, comparative analysis, pilot implementation, doctrinal development
Acknowledgments: Credits boyfriend Xiaoshu Luo, father Xianhui Zhang, [Zhao Peng], reviewers
Provides references, case law, legislation

Strengths in clarity; suggests rephrasing 'veil-piercing triggers' to 'triggers for disregarding contractual form'
Praises anecdote and vocabulary gap; critiques notification assumption and suggests acknowledging infrastructural limits; quibbles on anecdote specificity
